In [[mathematics]], '''Nemytskii operators''' are a class of [[nonlinear operator]]s on [[Lp space|''L''<sup>''p''</sup> spaces]] with good [[continuous function|continuity]] and [[bounded function|boundedness]] properties. They take their name from the [[mathematician]] [[Viktor Vladimirovich Nemytskii]].

==General definition of Superposition operator==

Let <math display="inline">\mathbb{X},\ \mathbb{Y},\ \mathbb{Z} \neq \varnothing</math> be non-empty sets. Let <math display="inline">\mathbb{Y}^ \mathbb{X},\ \mathbb{Z}^\mathbb{X}</math> denote the sets of mappings from <math display="inline">\mathbb{X}</math> to <math display="inline">\mathbb{Y}</math> and <math display="inline">\mathbb{Z}</math> respectively. 
Let <math display="inline">h\ \colon \mathbb{X} \times \mathbb{Y} \to \mathbb{Z}</math>.

Then the '''Nemytskii superposition operator''' <math display="inline">H\ \colon \mathbb{Y}^\mathbb{X} \to \mathbb{Z}^\mathbb{X}</math> induced by <math> h </math> is the map taking any map <math display="inline">\varphi \in \mathbb{Y}^\mathbb{X}</math> to the map <math display="inline">H\varphi \in \mathbb{Z}^\mathbb{X}</math> defined by
<math display="block">(H\varphi)(x) = h(x, \varphi(x)) \in \mathbb{Z}, \quad \mbox{for all}\ x\in \mathbb{X}.</math> 
The function <math display="inline">h</math> is called the '''generator''' of the Nemytskii operator <math display="inline">H</math>.

==Definition of Nemytskii operator==

Let &Omega; be a domain (an [[open set|open]] and [[connected space|connected set]]) in ''n''-dimensional [[Euclidean space]]. A function ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;&Omega;&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''m''</sup>&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R''' is said to satisfy the '''Carathéodory conditions''' if
* ''f''(''x'',&nbsp;''u'') is a continuous function of ''u'' for [[almost all]] ''x''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;&Omega;;
* ''f''(''x'',&nbsp;''u'') is a [[measurable function]] of ''x'' for all ''u''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''m''</sup>.

Given a function ''f'' satisfying the Carathéodory conditions and a function ''u''&nbsp;:&nbsp;&Omega;&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''m''</sup>, define a new function ''F''(''u'')&nbsp;:&nbsp;&Omega;&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R''' by

:<math>F(u)(x) = f \big( x, u(x) \big).</math>

The function ''F'' is called a '''Nemytskii operator'''.

== Theorem on Lipschitzian Operators ==

Suppose that <math display="inline">h: [a, b] \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}</math>, <math display="inline">X = \text{Lip} [a, b]</math> and

<math display="block">H: \text{Lip} [a, b] \to \text{Lip} [a, b]</math>

where the operator <math display="inline">H</math> is defined as <math display="inline">\left( Hf \right) \left(x\right)</math> <math display="inline">= h(x, f(x))</math> for any function <math display="inline">f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}</math> and any <math display="inline">x \in [a,b]</math>. Under these conditions the operator <math display="inline">H</math> is [[Lipschitz continuous]] if and only if there exist functions <math display="inline">G, H \in \text{Lip} [a, b]</math> such that

<math display="block">h(x, y) = G(x)y + H(x), \quad x \in [a, b], \quad y \in \mathbb{R}.</math>

==Boundedness theorem==

Let &Omega; be a domain, let 1&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;''p''&nbsp;&lt;&nbsp;+&infin; and let ''g''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;''L''<sup>''q''</sup>(&Omega;;&nbsp;'''R'''), with

:<math>\frac1{p} + \frac1{q} = 1.</math>

Suppose that ''f'' satisfies the Carathéodory conditions and that, for some constant ''C'' and all ''x'' and ''u'',

:<math>\big| f(x, u) \big| \leq C | u |^{p - 1} + g(x).</math>

Then the Nemytskii operator ''F'' as defined above is a bounded and continuous map from ''L''<sup>''p''</sup>(&Omega;;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''m''</sup>) into ''L''<sup>''q''</sup>(&Omega;;&nbsp;'''R''').
